text: I've met a lot of organizations that think most of their issues are in the training of their people. And 99% of the time I see that it's actually in the way that they're setting their goals and deploying their strategy.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Lenny asks Melissa about common problems she encounters when helping companies improve their product organizations. Melissa explains that most organizations mistakenly believe their problems stem from inadequate training of their product teams. However, she observes that the real issue is usually strategic - companies fail to set clear goals and deploy coherent strategies, leaving even well-trained employees without proper direction.
text_ko: 사람들에 대한 교육(training)에 문제가 있다고 생각하는 조직을 많이 만났어요. 그런데 제 경험상 99%는 실제 문제의 원인이 목표 설정(goals)과 전략 실행(strategy deployment)에 있어요. 사람들을 교육해도 그들이 무엇을 위해 일해야 하는지에 대한 맥락(context)이 없으면 소용이 없거든요.
text_zh: 我接触过很多公司，他们都觉得问题主要出在员工培训上。但我发现99%的情况下，真正的问题其实是他们设定目标和执行策略的方式有问题。因为你把人培训完了，他们根本不知道该朝哪个方向努力。
text_es: He conocido muchas organizaciones que creen que la mayoría de sus problemas están en la capacitación de su gente. Y el 99% de las veces me doy cuenta de que en realidad está en cómo están planteando sus objetivos y ejecutando su estrategia. Porque una vez que capacitas a esa gente, no tienen ni idea hacia dónde enfocar sus esfuerzos.
key_sentence: Issues often stem from deploying their strategy, not training people.
original_text: I've met a lot of organizations that think most of their issues are in the training of their people. And 99% of the time I see that it's actually in the way that they're setting their goals and deploying their strategy. Because once you train those people, they have no context on what to work towards.

vocabulary.definition: The act of putting a plan, resource, or strategy into action or operation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, deploying often refers to the implementation of software, marketing strategies, or operational processes to achieve specific objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While deploying implies a systematic and organized approach, it can also suggest a level of urgency or necessity in execution.

vocabulary.definition: A carefully devised plan of action designed to achieve a specific goal or set of objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, strategy encompasses long-term planning and decision-making that guides an organization towards its vision and competitive advantage.
vocabulary.nuance: The term strategy often implies a comprehensive and well-thought-out approach, distinguishing it from mere tactics or short-term actions.

vocabulary.definition: The process of establishing specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound objectives to guide performance and progress.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, setting goals is crucial for aligning team efforts, measuring success, and motivating employees towards common objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While setting goals is essential for direction, poorly defined goals can lead to confusion and misalignment within an organization.

vocabulary.definition: Structured groups of individuals working together to achieve common goals, often characterized by defined roles, responsibilities, and hierarchies.
vocabulary.businessContext: Organizations can range from small startups to large corporations, and they play a critical role in the economy by providing goods, services, and employment.
vocabulary.nuance: The term organization can imply a formal structure, but it can also encompass informal groups or networks that collaborate towards shared interests.

text: it's such a holistic approach when you actually go through these transformations... you either need somebody in there to do it, or you've got to really be ready to move when somebody comes in to help you.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Melissa continues explaining why product transformations are challenging. She emphasizes that building an effective product organization requires a comprehensive approach that addresses multiple interconnected elements - not just training people, but also establishing proper goal-setting and strategy deployment. Companies need either internal leadership capable of driving this transformation or external help, but they must be prepared to take decisive action.
text_ko: 실제로 이런 변화(transformation)를 겪거나 프로덕트 조직(product organization)을 구성하려고 할 땐 전체적인 접근(holistic approach)이 필요해요. 그래서 그걸 직접 해줄 내부 인력이 있든가, 외부에서 도우러 왔을 때 바로 움직일 준비가 돼 있어야 해요.
text_zh: 所以当你真正要做这些转型，或者想要搭建产品组织的时候，这其实是一个很全面的方法，要么你得有人在内部来做这个事儿，要么你得做好准备，等有人来帮你的时候能够马上行动起来。
text_es: Entonces es un enfoque realmente integral cuando pasas por estas transformaciones, o cuando tratas de montar una organización de producto, así que o necesitas a alguien interno que lo haga, or tienes que estar listo para moverte cuando llegue alguien de afuera para echarte la mano.
key_sentence: it's such a holistic approach when you actually go through these transformations
original_text: So it's such a holistic approach when you actually go through these transformations, or try to set up a product organization, so you either need somebody in there to do it, or you've got to really be ready to move when somebody comes in to help you.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to or concerned with complete systems rather than individual parts; emphasizing the interconnectedness of various components.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a holistic approach often refers to strategies that consider all aspects of an organization, including culture, processes, and stakeholder relationships, to achieve overall effectiveness.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'holistic' suggests a comprehensive view, it may imply a lack of focus on specific details, so it should be used when discussing integrated strategies rather than isolated tactics.

vocabulary.definition: Significant changes or alterations in form, appearance, nature, or character, often leading to improved performance or outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, transformations can refer to organizational changes, such as digital transformation, which enhances efficiency and competitiveness in the market.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a positive connotation, suggesting growth and improvement, and is often used in discussions about innovation and change management.

vocabulary.definition: Including all or nearly all elements or aspects; thorough and complete in scope.
vocabulary.businessContext: A comprehensive business plan outlines every detail of a company's strategy, including market analysis, financial projections, and operational plans, ensuring all stakeholders are informed.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'comprehensive' implies thoroughness, it can also suggest complexity, so it should be used when emphasizing the need for detailed and all-encompassing information.

vocabulary.definition: Successful in producing a desired or intended result; capable of achieving goals efficiently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, effective strategies or practices lead to improved performance, higher productivity, and better customer satisfaction, making them essential for success.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'effective' focuses on outcomes, it can sometimes overlook the processes involved, so it should be used when results are the primary concern rather than methods.

text: At that point, they have to rethink their entire strategy.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Lenny asks about common problems at modern tech companies that Melissa encounters in her consulting work. Melissa describes the critical junction point when SaaS companies transition from finding product-market fit to scaling up. At this stage, companies face the challenge of managing a complex portfolio while having numerous feature requests from existing customers, making strategic focus and prioritization essential for success.
text_ko: 그때가 되면 전체 전략을 다시 생각해야 해요. 선택지가 너무 많아서 기존 고객을 위해 계속 개발해 나갈지, 모두가 요청하는 걸 다 백로그(backlog)에서 꺼내 처리할지 결정하려면 정말 집중해서 우선순위를 정해야 해요.
text_zh: 到了那个时候，他们就得重新想整个战略了。然后必须得聚焦，因为他们有太多选择了——既要为现有客户继续开发功能，又要处理积压需求(backlog)里的一堆需求，大家都在提各种要求，所以真的必须得重点突出，分清轻重缓急。
text_es: En ese momento, tienen que replantearse toda su estrategia. Y después tienen que enfocarse porque tienen un montón de opciones para seguir desarrollando cosas para sus clientes actuales y sacar todo del backlog porque todos están pidiendo cosas, realmente tienen que enfocarse y priorizar.
key_sentence: they have to rethink their entire strategy.
original_text: At that point, they have to rethink their entire strategy. And then they have to focus because they have all of these choices to keep building for their existing customers and just take everything off the backlog because everybody's requesting things, they really have to focus and prioritize.

vocabulary.definition: To reconsider or reevaluate a decision, plan, or approach in light of new information or circumstances.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, 'rethink' is often used when organizations need to adjust their strategies or operations to better align with market changes or internal assessments.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'rethink' implies a significant change in perspective, it can also suggest a more thoughtful and deliberate approach rather than a hasty decision.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim, often involving the allocation of resources and setting priorities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, a 'strategy' outlines how a company intends to compete in the market, including its goals, target audience, and methods for achieving success.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'strategy' often conveys a sense of foresight and planning, suggesting a comprehensive approach rather than a series of isolated actions.

vocabulary.definition: Of great importance or significance; essential to the success or failure of a situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'critical' often refers to key factors or decisions that can determine the outcome of projects, initiatives, or overall company performance.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'critical' can imply urgency, it also suggests a need for careful analysis and consideration, especially in high-stakes environments.

vocabulary.definition: The process of changing from one state or condition to another, often involving adjustments in operations, strategies, or structures.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'transition' is commonly used to describe shifts such as organizational changes, market adaptations, or the implementation of new technologies.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'transition' often carries a connotation of gradual change, suggesting that the process may require time and careful management to ensure success.

text: A big sign for me, when I've come into organizations to help CEOs where they're like, do we need a product person to oversee this? I don't know what a product person does.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Lenny asks when it's time for a company to hire a Chief Product Officer (CPO). Melissa explains that a key indicator is when CEOs and executives feel disconnected from their product and technology teams. When leadership doesn't understand what's happening in product development or whether goals are being achieved, it signals the need for a senior product leader who can serve as a strategic partner to the CEO and communicate effectively with the board and executive team.
text_ko: 제가 CEO들을 도와 조직에 들어갈 때마다 한 가지 확실한 신호가 있어요. "이걸 감독할 프로덕트 담당자(product person)가 필요할까? 그 사람이 뭘 하는지도 잘 모르겠네"라고 말할 때요. 저는 보통 "지금 어떤 문제들이 있으세요?" 하고 물어보고, 그들이 겪는 걸 다 얘기하게 해요. 그러면 "아, 이 문제들 중 상당수는 사실 그 역할을 같이해 줄 파트너가 없어서 생긴 거예요"라고 말하곤 해요.
text_zh: 我进入一些公司帮助CEO的时候，经常会遇到一个很明显的信号，就是他们会问我，我们是不是需要找个产品人员来负责这块？说实话我也不太清楚产品人员具体是干什么的。这时候我通常会跟他们聊，问他们现在遇到什么挑战？他们会跟我说一大堆问题，然后我就会告诉他们，其实你们说的这些问题，很多都是因为你们缺少一个能配合你们工作的合作伙伴造成的。
text_es: Una señal muy clara para mí, cuando llego a organizaciones para ayudar a CEOs que me dicen, ¿necesitamos a alguien de producto para supervisar esto? No sé qué hace una persona de producto. Y normalmente los voy guiando con preguntas como, oye, ¿cuáles son los retos que están enfrentando? Me cuentan todo, y yo les digo, okay, estos problemas en realidad se deben a que no tienen ese socio estratégico (partner) con quien trabajar.
key_sentence: I don't know what a product person does.
original_text: A big sign for me, when I've come into organizations to help CEOs where they're like, do we need a product person to oversee this? I don't know what a product person does. And I usually talk them through like, hey, what are the challenges you're having? And they tell me everything, and I'm like, okay, these ones are actually caused by you not having that partner to work with.

vocabulary.definition: A sign or piece of information that suggests the state or level of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, indicators are often used to measure performance, such as key performance indicators (KPIs) that help assess the success of an organization or project.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'indicator' can refer to any sign, in business it often implies a quantitative measure that informs decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: To supervise or manage a process, project, or group of people to ensure that tasks are completed effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, executives often oversee departments or initiatives, ensuring that objectives align with the company's strategic goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a level of authority and responsibility, often associated with higher management roles.

vocabulary.definition: Not connected or lacking a coherent relationship with something else.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, a disconnected team may struggle with communication and collaboration, leading to inefficiencies and misunderstandings.
vocabulary.nuance: This term can carry a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of integration or synergy within an organization.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals in high-level management positions responsible for making major decisions and overseeing the operations of an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: Executives play a crucial role in strategic planning and resource allocation, often setting the direction for the entire company.
vocabulary.nuance: The term typically connotes authority and influence, and is often associated with senior leadership roles such as CEOs, CFOs, and COOs.

text: And I would try to ladder that up myself into a strategy and see if it was connected. And if it wasn't connected, that's telling me somebody's not formulating the strategy and deploying it down.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Melissa describes her diagnostic process when consulting with companies. She asks individual teams what they're working on and why, then attempts to connect their work to an overarching strategy. When she can't make these connections, it indicates that either no comprehensive strategy exists at the executive level, or the strategy isn't being effectively communicated and deployed throughout the organization.
text_ko: 저는 그걸 제가 직접 상위 전략으로 연결해(ladder up) 보고 실제로 연결돼 있는지 확인해요. 만약 연결돼 있지 않다면, 그건 누군가 전략을 제대로 수립해서 하향 전개(deploy down)하지 않았다는 신호예요. 결국 최고위층에 전략이 부족하다는 뜻이에요.
text_zh: 然后我会试着把这些往上串联成一个完整的战略，看看它们之间有没有关联。如果发现没什么关联的话，那就说明上面的人没有制定好战略，也没有往下传达执行。这就告诉我，高层缺乏战略思维。
text_es: Y yo trataría de conectar eso hacia arriba con la estrategia para ver si había coherencia. Y si no estaba conectado, eso me dice que alguien no está formulando bien la estrategia ni bajándola a los equipos. Y entonces ahí me doy cuenta de que falta estrategia clara desde arriba.
key_sentence: if it wasn't connected, that's telling me somebody's not formulating the strategy and deploying it down.
original_text: And I would try to ladder that up myself into a strategy and see if it was connected. And if it wasn't connected, that's telling me somebody's not formulating the strategy and deploying it down. And then, that's telling me there is a lack of strategy at the top.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim, often involving the allocation of resources.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a strategy outlines how an organization intends to compete in the market, addressing aspects like product development, marketing, and customer engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'strategy' implies a comprehensive and thoughtful approach, it can sometimes be perceived as overly theoretical if not backed by actionable steps.

vocabulary.definition: The process of creating or devising a plan or strategy in a systematic manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, formulating involves the careful consideration of various factors to develop effective strategies or policies.
vocabulary.nuance: This term suggests a methodical and thoughtful approach, often implying that the outcome is based on research and analysis.

vocabulary.definition: The act of putting a plan, strategy, or resource into effective action or operation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, deploying can refer to the implementation of software, marketing strategies, or operational plans to achieve desired outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often conveys a sense of readiness and execution, emphasizing the transition from planning to action.

vocabulary.definition: Having a relationship or link with something else, often implying coherence or relevance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, being connected can refer to the alignment of strategies, goals, or systems that work together to enhance overall effectiveness.
vocabulary.nuance: This term suggests a positive relationship and synergy, and is often used to highlight the importance of integration in business operations.

text: But if we think about all the things that teams do in isolation, it's not enough, usually, to move those business metrics. So what people do in a lack of strategy is they spread the team too thin across tons of initiatives.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Melissa explains what happens when companies lack proper strategy deployment. She describes how individual teams might be working on various features and enhancements, but when these efforts aren't coordinated toward common strategic goals, they fail to create meaningful business impact. Without strategic focus, organizations tend to scatter their resources across too many initiatives, preventing any single effort from achieving significant results.
text_ko: 하지만 팀이 각자 따로따로 일하는 것만으로는 보통 비즈니스 지표(business metrics)를 충분히 움직이기 어려워요. 그래서 전략이 없으면 사람들은 팀을 너무 얇게 쪼개 여러 이니셔티브(initiatives)에 투입해요. 한 팀만으로는 보통 큰 임팩트를 주는 핵심 지표(core metrics)를 개선하기에 부족해요.
text_zh: 但是你想想，如果团队各自为政、单打独斗的话，通常是很难推动那些关键业务指标的。所以很多人在缺乏策略的情况下，就会让团队在一大堆项目上摊得太开，精力分散。光靠一个团队，通常是很难做出那种真正有冲击力的数据表现的。
text_es: Pero si pensamos en todas las cosas que los equipos hacen por separado, normalmente no es suficiente para mover esas métricas del negocio. Entonces lo que pasa cuando no hay una estrategia clara es que dispersan al equipo en demasiadas iniciativas a la vez. Un solo equipo generalmente no basta para conseguir métricas realmente contundentes.
key_sentence: Teams spread too thin fail to achieve hard hitting metrics.
original_text: But if we think about all the things that teams do in isolation, it's not enough, usually, to move those business metrics. So what people do in a lack of strategy is they spread the team too thin across tons of initiatives. One team usually isn't enough to get some really hard hitting metrics out there.

vocabulary.definition: Quantifiable measures used to track and assess the status of a business's performance over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, metrics such as revenue growth, customer acquisition cost, and net promoter score are critical for evaluating success and informing strategic decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a focus on data-driven decision-making, and should be used when discussing performance evaluation rather than qualitative assessments.

vocabulary.definition: The absence of a clear plan or approach to achieve specific goals or objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, a lack of strategy can lead to misalignment of resources and efforts, resulting in inefficiencies and missed opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often carries a negative connotation, suggesting disorganization or poor leadership, and should be used to highlight deficiencies in planning.

vocabulary.definition: To overextend oneself or a team by taking on too many tasks or responsibilities at once.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and businesses, spreading a team too thin can lead to burnout, decreased productivity, and lower quality of work, as resources are insufficient to meet demands.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often implies a warning against overcommitment and should be used when discussing workload management and resource allocation.

vocabulary.definition: Strategic actions or projects undertaken to achieve specific objectives or drive change within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, initiatives can range from new product launches to process improvements, and are often critical for driving growth and innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a proactive approach and is typically used in a positive context, though it can imply a lack of focus if there are too many initiatives at once.

text: And the best teams I've ever seen, the most successful companies I've ever seen, everybody works together, and they're like, these are our goals, and these are our business goals.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Lenny asks about signs that indicate a company has good strategy in place. Melissa describes what effective strategy deployment looks like - when executives function as a unified team with aligned goals rather than competing against each other. She contrasts this with dysfunctional organizations where different departments have conflicting priorities, explaining that successful companies achieve cross-functional alignment around shared business objectives.
text_ko: 제가 본 최고의 팀들과 가장 성공한 회사들은 다 같이 협업해요. 모두가 '이게 우리의 목표고, 이게 비즈니스 목표(business goals)예요'라고 공감해요. 그래서 전략(strategy)이 제대로 실행되고 경영진(executives)에게도 그런 문화가 자리 잡으면, 모두가 같은 방향을 보고 있어요.
text_zh: 我见过的最好的团队，最成功的那些公司，大家都是拧成一股绳，就像，这是咱们的目标，这是咱们的业务目标。所以当战略部署到位，再加上高管层都有这种文化氛围，大家想法都特别一致。
text_es: Y los mejores equipos que he visto, las empresas más exitosas que conozco, todos trabajan en conjunto, y están como que "estos son nuestros objetivos, estas son nuestras metas del negocio." Entonces cuando la estrategia se ejecuta bien y tienes ese tipo de cultura también, con tus ejecutivos, todos están en la misma sintonía.
key_sentence: everybody works together, and they're like, these are our goals, and these are our business goals.
original_text: And the best teams I've ever seen, the most successful companies I've ever seen, everybody works together, and they're like, these are our goals, and these are our business goals. So when strategy is deployed correctly and you have that type of culture, too, with your executives, they're all on the same page.

vocabulary.definition: In agreement or cooperation with a particular goal or standard.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being aligned often refers to teams or departments working towards the same objectives, ensuring that efforts are coordinated and effective.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'aligned' suggests harmony and cooperation, it can also imply a lack of independent thought or creativity if used too rigidly.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, strategy involves the formulation of plans that guide an organization’s direction, resource allocation, and competitive positioning.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'strategy' carries a connotation of careful planning and foresight, and should not be confused with short-term tactics or operational decisions.

vocabulary.definition: Formed or brought together into a single entity or group.
vocabulary.businessContext: A unified team in a business context indicates that all members are working cohesively towards shared objectives, which can enhance productivity and morale.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'unified' suggests strength in collaboration, it may also imply a suppression of individual perspectives or dissenting opinions.

vocabulary.definition: Specific objectives or targets that an individual or organization aims to achieve.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, goals are critical for setting direction and measuring success, often categorized into short-term and long-term objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'goals' can imply a sense of ambition and purpose, but may also suggest rigidity if not approached with flexibility in execution.
